Log-Likelihood, Covariance and Number of Observations of a Fit

Source: R/auxiliary.R
logLik.RiskMap.Rd

The logLik(), vcov() and nobs() methods for fits from glgpm(), with which stats::AIC() and stats::BIC() work too.

Usage

# S3 method for class 'RiskMap'
logLik(object, ...)

# S3 method for class 'RiskMap'
vcov(object, ...)

# S3 method for class 'RiskMap'
nobs(object, ...)

Arguments

object

A fit from glgpm().

...

Not used, and an error if given, so that a misspelt argument is not ignored.

Value

logLik() gives an object of class logLik, vcov() a matrix and nobs() an integer.

Details

logLik() gives the log-likelihood at the estimates. It is exact for a Gaussian model. For a binomial, Poisson or negative binomial model it is a Monte Carlo estimate, so that differences between such models that are not well above its Monte Carlo error mean nothing, which is why summary() gives no AIC for them. That of a negative binomial model leaves out the terms that do not depend on the parameters, as that of a Poisson model does (see negative_binomial()). Its degrees of freedom, df, are the number of estimated parameters, without those that fixed_pars holds.

vcov() gives the covariance matrix of the estimates on the scale of coef(), by the delta method from their covariance on the scale on which the model is fitted, where the variances and the scale are on the log scale. Its rows and columns are named as unlist(coef(object)) names them, for the estimated parameters only. A parameter without a standard error, such as a variance estimated at zero, has a row and a column of NA, and a fit that holds every parameter has an empty matrix.

nobs() gives the number of observations, the rows of the data, whatever their denominators.

See also

summary.RiskMap() for standard errors and confidence intervals.

Examples

data(italy_sim)

fit <- glgpm(
  formula = y ~ gp(),
  data = italy_sim[1:100,],
  family = "gaussian",
  messages = FALSE
)

logLik(fit)
#> 'log Lik.' 8.618636 (df=4)
AIC(fit)
#> [1] -9.237272
vcov(fit)
#>                  beta.(Intercept)        sigma2           phi     sigma2_me
#> beta.(Intercept)     6.853929e-01 -1.185935e-01 -5.836712e+00  3.579153e-07
#> sigma2              -1.185935e-01  5.882057e+00  5.605035e+01 -7.744215e-05
#> phi                 -5.836712e+00  5.605035e+01  2.766884e+03  5.171587e-04
#> sigma2_me            3.579153e-07 -7.744215e-05  5.171587e-04  7.087906e-04
nobs(fit)
#> [1] 100
